result.title: NormTune: Norm-Guided Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Reasoning-Intensive Tasks
result.summary: Full fine-tuning has achieved remarkable success on reasoning-intensive tasks, but it often requires substantial GPU resource consumption. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) provides a promising alternative for reducing this cost, yet we observe a substantial performance gap on reasoning-intensive tasks. In this paper, we present three key observations showing that this gap is closely associated with norm-related under-adaptation, where PEFT produces markedly smaller weight-update norms than full fine-tuning. Based on these observations, we propose Norm-Guided Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (NormTune), a simple yet effective strategy that adaptively strengthens insufficiently updated layers according to their weight-update norms. Extensive experiments show that NormTune consistently enhances multiple PEFT methods across challenging reasoning benchmarks. Specifically, when trained on S1K-1.1, integrating NormTune into rank-8 LoRA, Bone, and MoRA yields substantial average accuracy improvements of 24.24\%, 11.33\%, and 16.21\% , respectively, across AIME 2024, MATH 500, GPQA, and AIME 2025. Moreover, NormTune-enhanced rank-256 LoRA, Bone, and MoRA achieve performance comparable to S1 full fine-tuning, with respective average gains of 2.17\%, 0.93\%, and 3.00\% over this baseline.

AI.brief_summary: 论文观察到 PEFT 在推理密集任务上出现权重更新范数显著偏小的「适配不足」，据此提出 NormTune，按各层权重更新范数自适应加强对更新不足的层，并在多种 PEFT 方法与数学、科学推理基准上报告稳定提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究对象是纯文本推理的 PEFT 效率，与视觉 latent 推理无直接关联；但「用权重更新范数诊断适配是否充分、并按层调节更新强度」这一线索可供核查能否用于判断 VLM 推理或 latent 轨迹训练中 LoRA 是否真正改动关键层。
